analysis.title: From AI Mania To EM Capitulation (The Setup For A Reversal)
key_insights: EEM has fallen sharply since late June, when the note called it a giant Asia AI bet driven by semiconductors, speculation and leverage. It now trades well below its 200-day moving average with momentum still weak.
Selling has spread beyond equities. Per BofA, EM debt funds had their sixth-largest weekly outflow on record.
EEM is approaching major support levels, and weekly RSI is at its lowest since November 2022. The note frames the extreme selling as a possible setup for a reversal.
Tech and commodities are both under pressure, so EEM is being hit from both sides. The commodity link to the index remains in place.
EEM's rally earlier this year came with a sharp rise in volatility (spot up, vol up). The current sell-off has also lifted volatility, but with spot falling.
The VXEEM-VIX gap is large and is driven by downside fear, where earlier in the year it was driven by upside fear. VXEEM tracks KOSPI volatility closely.
Earlier sharp pullbacks in EEM, including some with RSI above the current level, were followed by strong reversals higher.
risk_factors: Further EM equity and debt liquidation if EEM breaks the support level it is approaching.
Continued pressure on both the tech and commodity drivers of EM equities.
Emerging-market selling spreading beyond equities into debt funds.
vol_and_positioning: VXEEM has surged as EEM sold off, with spot moving sharply lower, unlike the earlier spot-up, vol-up pattern.
The VXEEM vs VIX gap is large and reflects downside fear. The note says VXEEM tracks KOSPI volatility closely.
BofA data: EM debt funds had their sixth-largest weekly outflow on record.
EEM weekly RSI is at its lowest level since November 2022.
